evals.prompt: Any new agent frameworks worth knowing about? Fold anything good into the AI tooling catalog.
evals.expected_output: The ai-engineering-update skill is invoked: seed sources and/or web research surface candidates, each is verified (what it is, status, license) before classification, findings are piped through ledger.py ingest (duplicates report unchanged), new triage rows are classified via seed-sections.tsv or rules.tsv, link-ledger.md is regenerated via ledger.py render, and a summary reports counts added/reclassified/unchanged.
expectations: The ai-engineering-update skill is invoked
Discovery uses the seed sources and/or WebSearch/deep-research, and candidate repos are verified (purpose, status, license) before being classified
New URLs are added via ledger.py ingest, with already-known links reporting unchanged rather than being re-added
Any new triage rows are classified by editing seed-sections.tsv or rules.tsv (data edits), then re-ingested - not by editing ledger.py code
link-ledger.md is regenerated with ledger.py render and is never hand-edited
The final report summarizes counts: added, unchanged/duplicates, reclassified, and any opinion changes worth noting

evals.prompt: Check the AI tooling catalog for staleness and dead links.
evals.expected_output: The ai-engineering-update skill is invoked and runs the freshness pass: ledger.py check with a TTL and --probe flags stale/dead rows, dead rows are investigated (moved/renamed/abandoned) and flagged non-destructively, and the ledger is re-rendered with a summary of what changed.
expectations: The ai-engineering-update skill is invoked
ledger.py check is run with a --ttl value and --probe (optionally --limit) to flag stale rows and mark dead ones
Rows found dead are investigated and updated or flagged, not silently deleted - catalog rows for abandoned projects get a status/caution, preserving history
ledger.py render is run afterward to regenerate link-ledger.md
The report states how many rows were stale, how many dead, and what was done about each

evals.prompt: Add these AI links to the catalog: https://github.com/example-org/agent-kit and https://example-tool.dev/docs
evals.expected_output: The ai-engineering-update skill is invoked and the links are ingested through the deterministic engine: ledger.py ingest canonicalizes and dedupes them, any GitHub repo without a seed-sections entry lands in triage and gets classified via a seed-sections.tsv (or rules.tsv) row, and link-ledger.md is regenerated.
expectations: The ai-engineering-update skill is invoked
The URLs are added via ledger.py ingest rather than by hand-editing catalog files or link-ledger.md
Duplicate handling is honored: a link already in the catalog is reported unchanged, not re-added

A GitHub/DeepWiki repo landing in triage is classified by adding an owner/repo → sections row to seed-sections.tsv (or a domain rule to rules.tsv) using the existing section vocabulary, then re-ingested or set
ledger.py render is run and the report states which links were new versus already known

evals.prompt: Update our npm dependencies to their latest versions and fix anything that breaks.
evals.expected_output: The ai-engineering-update skill is NOT invoked; this is a project dependency upgrade, not maintenance of the AI tooling catalog. The agent performs a normal dependency update workflow (package manager commands, run tests, fix breakage) without touching ledger.py or the catalog files.
expectations: The ai-engineering-update skill is NOT invoked
ledger.py is not run and no catalog files (catalog.tsv, seed-sections.tsv, rules.tsv, link-ledger.md) are read or modified
The agent handles it as a standard dependency upgrade: package manager update commands, followed by running the test suite and fixing any breakage

evals.prompt: Heads up, LightRAG fell over on us today - it OOMed once we passed about 50k documents on a 16GB box. Worth remembering.
evals.expected_output: The ai-engineering-update skill is invoked for its record job: the observation is written as a field note via ledger.py field-note against LightRAG's catalogued URL, with a verdict of broken or caution, the finding stated in one line, and the scope carrying the condition it held under (roughly 50k documents, 16GB). The agent does not edit field-notes.tsv or field-notes.md by hand, and does not delete or overwrite any existing note about the tool.
expectations: The ai-engineering-update skill is invoked, without waiting for a scheduled maintenance pass
The observation is recorded with ledger.py field-note against the tool's canonical catalogued URL, not by hand-editing field-notes.tsv or the generated field-notes.md
A verdict from the closed set (works, caution, broken, superseded) is chosen, and the scope field carries the condition the finding held under rather than being left blank
Existing notes about the tool are left intact - the store is append-only, so a new observation never overwrites an earlier one
The agent does not silently promote the observation into agent-stack-map.md as if it were researched third-party fact

evals.prompt: Go re-verify the harnesses section of the AI stack map - I don't trust those star counts and licenses any more.
evals.expected_output: The verify job runs against the claims queue rather than the liveness probe: ledger.py check --claims --section harnesses produces the work list, each row is re-verified against a live source, agent-stack-map.md is corrected with dates, and only the rows actually checked are stamped with ledger.py verified.
expectations: The claims queue is used (ledger.py check --claims, scoped by section) rather than the liveness probe, which only establishes that a URL resolves
Rows are re-verified against a live source rather than from training memory
agent-stack-map.md is corrected with the verification date attached to each changed claim
Only rows that were actually checked get stamped with ledger.py verified - the date is the value of the field
A figure that cannot be confirmed is left as verify rather than filled with a plausible number
